current: The position of the literature with respect to Req 3 can therefore be stated precisely.
replacement: The position of the literature with respect to Req 3 can therefore be stated precisely. Multi-party authorisation exists in the six mechanism classes ratified by the coding panel. The first is joint approval on a contingency path when the principal is absent, with key-share reconstruction among guardians, custodians or relatives [53, 35, 54]. The second is an institution-side threshold over record admission and consent revocation [75]. The third is a consumer-side delegated threshold [50]. The fourth is a patient-appointed witness threshold bound to key release [69]. The fifth is custodial M-of-N approval placed around, but not inside, a policy predicate [61]. The sixth is guardian co-consent at the time of consent registration [43, 47], with the bilateral co-signature of Al Amin et al. [38] recorded as a candidate of this class. In this context, the statement that multi-party authorisation does not exist in the literature is no longer defensible and is not made in this review. What does not exist in any of the 44 included studies is a threshold predicate over the guardian set G with threshold N that is constitutive of the access decision. Such a predicate would be evaluated on every access request in a decentralised exchange, as a conjunct of the same predicate that evaluates the purpose and data scope, the temporal validity and the jurisdiction of the consent object C, with allow and deny correctness evidence and formal assurance of the conjunction. The coding supports each element of this statement. Only Punia et al. [61] combine T3 = Yes with an enforced policy predicate, and there the threshold is outside the predicate, the patient is an attribute and purpose is absent. Every T3-positive study in this stream is graded No or Partial on Req 6. The two T3-positive studies elsewhere that carry a proof [50, 54] prove the threshold gate or confidentiality in isolation, so that the broadest multi-party systems carry the weakest assurance. In addition, the deployed guardian mechanisms [43, 47] establish guardian authority through a state register, which is the attestation pattern against which the guardian credentials of the proposed framework must be compared. Table 5 presents a summary of the eight analysed studies in this stream and their commitment to the key requirements.
